"""Private path ownership for the durable SQLite store (DE03a); not exported.

One canonical database path has one owner process from opening through closing
(plan §3.1). The owner holds an exclusive ``flock`` on a never-deleted
``<database>.lock`` sidecar. The lock is not taken on the database file itself:
on macOS a ``flock`` there makes SQLite's own ``fcntl`` locking report
"database is locked". Lock contents are diagnostics only and never decide
ownership; a crashed owner's lock is released by the kernel, and nothing is
ever stolen by age.

Aliases meet the same lock: the parent directory is resolved with ``realpath``
and the file name kept, so symlinked or relative directories and ``..`` reach
one directory, and case variants on a case-insensitive volume reach the same
lock inode. The final database name must not be a symbolic link, and a
database, sidecar or lock file with a second hard link is refused, since its
other names would carry different lock and journal names. Within one process, a
registry of lock inodes and claimed database inodes refuses a second owner
before ``flock`` is consulted. Every descriptor is close-on-exec. In a forked
child, the ``register_at_fork`` hook closes the inherited lock and parked
descriptor copies, poisons every inherited owner and pins inherited SQLite
connections so they are never finalized there: a child finalizing an inherited
WAL connection after its owner's clean close deletes a later owner's crash-left
WAL by name (probed on macOS and Linux), losing committed rows.

Owner-only files: missing parent directories are created ``0o700``; the
database is created ``O_EXCL`` and set to ``0o600`` whatever the umask, and
SQLite gives its ``-wal``, ``-shm`` and ``-journal`` the database's mode.
Existing files with group or other bits are set to ``0o600`` when they are
regular, owned by this user, readable and writable by it and have one link;
anything else is refused (Root decision D5). Shared and network filesystems are
refused before any filesystem effect (D8): macOS requires ``MNT_LOCAL`` on APFS
or HFS+, Linux a local filesystem type from the mount table entry of the
directory's own mount. ``create`` and ``open`` are explicit (D9): ``create``
refuses an existing database or stale SQLite sidecar (SQLite would silently
delete stale sidecars next to a new empty database), ``open`` refuses a missing
database, and invalid input or an ``open`` of a missing path changes nothing on
disk.

POSIX record locks, an invariant for every DE03 slice: closing any descriptor
of a file releases every POSIX record lock this process holds on it, SQLite's
included, whichever descriptor took them. So this module never opens a
descriptor of a store file another owner in this process holds: a second open
whose lock inode or database inode (by ``lstat``) is owned here is refused
before any descriptor on a store file is opened. Every owner claims its
database inode in the registry before it connects, and a claim never moves to
another inode. As belt and braces, every descriptor on an existing store file
is opened under the registry lock and identified by ``fstat`` first; one that
reached a database another owner here claimed is parked on that owner and
closed only in the registry lock hold that drops that claim, after the owner's
connection is closed. ``flock`` belongs to one open file description, so
closing another descriptor of the lock file never releases it (Linux emulates
``flock`` with POSIX locks only on NFS, which is refused). A second SQLite
connection to an owned store from the owning process is outside the contract.

Contract boundary. The store directory is private to the owning user (owned by
that user, mode ``0700``; missing directories are created that way, and keeping
an existing one private is the caller's part). While any owner holds a store,
from the moment an open or create of it starts until its close has completed,
renaming, replacing, hard-linking or deleting any store file (the database, its
``-wal``, ``-shm`` and ``-journal``, and the lock file), by any actor, is
outside the contract. pipy detects some of these cases on a best-effort basis
(the identity checks under the lock, after connecting and after configuration;
the parking of descriptors that reach a claimed database; the re-check before
each unlink of a failed create) but guarantees nothing about them. SQLite's own
guidance is the same: do not rename, unlink or replace an open database or its
journal. With the store files left in place, the guarantees hold: one owner per
store across processes and within the process, owner-only file modes, no
descriptor of a store file held by another owner in this process is ever closed
by pipy, and invalid input, an ``open`` of a missing path and a store refused
before its lock is taken have no filesystem effect. Pi durable 1.3.0 has no
cross-process locking at all, so this remains strictly stronger than the
reference.

Pi durable 1.3.0 has no path lock, file modes or filesystem checks
(``packages/durable/README.md``: "One process owns a storage at a time; there
is no cross-process locking"); this module is pipy's own.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import errno
import fcntl
import functools
import importlib.metadata
import json
import os
import stat
import sys
import threading
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Literal

from .storage import StorageClosedError

OpenMode = Literal["create", "open"]
# Checks an existing database through a read-only descriptor before any
# connection exists, given the size of its -wal by lstat (0 when there is none),
# raising to refuse it; the descriptor is not kept.
ExistingCheck = Callable[[int, str, int], None]

LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"
SIDECARS = ("-wal", "-shm", "-journal")
FILE_MODE = 0o600
DIRECTORY_MODE = 0o700

# Longest sidecar suffix; NAME_MAX is 255 bytes on the supported filesystems.
_NAME_MAX = 255
_LONGEST_SUFFIX = max(len(suffix) for suffix in (LOCK_SUFFIX, *SIDECARS))
_DIAGNOSTIC_LIMIT = 4096
# A variable, not a literal sys.platform check, so both branches type-check.
_PLATFORM = sys.platform
_DARWIN_MNT_LOCAL = 0x1000
_DARWIN_LOCAL_TYPES = frozenset({"apfs", "hfs"})
_LINUX_LOCAL_TYPES = frozenset(
    {
        "bcachefs",
        "btrfs",
        "ext2",
        "ext3",
        "ext4",
        "f2fs",
        "jfs",
        "nilfs2",
        "reiserfs",
        "tmpfs",
        "xfs",
        "zfs",
    }
)
_READ_FLAGS = os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC | os.O_NONBLOCK
_DIRECTORY_FLAGS = os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC


class StoragePathError(ValueError):
    """The path cannot hold a private durable store."""


class StorageNotFoundError(StoragePathError):
    """``open`` found no database at the path."""


class StorageExistsError(StoragePathError):
    """``create`` found an existing database or SQLite sidecar."""


class UnsupportedStoragePath(StoragePathError):
    """A file or filesystem at the path cannot be owned privately."""


class StorageOwnershipError(RuntimeError):
    """Another owner holds the path: another process, or this one via any alias."""


class StorageForkedError(RuntimeError):
    """An owner inherited through fork() cannot be used in the child."""


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class StoragePath:
    """Canonical directory (no symbolic links) and the database file name."""

    directory: str
    name: str

    @property
    def database(self) -> str:
        return os.path.join(self.directory, self.name)

    @property
    def lock(self) -> str:
        return self.database + LOCK_SUFFIX

    def sidecar(self, suffix: str) -> str:
        return self.database + suffix


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class StoreRequest:
    """Admitted caller input: exact built-in values only, nothing resolved yet."""

    head: str
    name: str
    mode: OpenMode


@dataclass(eq=False, slots=True)
class _Held:
    """Registry record of one held lock; mutated only under ``_REGISTRY_LOCK``."""

    key: tuple[int, int]
    fd: int
    pid: int
    # The owned database inode, claimed before this owner connects.
    database: tuple[int, int] | None = None
    # Descriptors of that inode a refused open reached; closing them before
    # this owner's connection is closed would drop its SQLite locks.
    parked: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
    # Objects a forked child must never finalize (inherited SQLite connections).
    pinned: list[object] = field(default_factory=list)


_REGISTRY_LOCK = threading.Lock()
_REGISTRY: dict[tuple[int, int], _Held] = {}


def _owned_here(lock: tuple[int, int] | None, database: tuple[int, int] | None) -> bool:
    """Whether this process already owns the lock inode or the database inode.

    The caller holds ``_REGISTRY_LOCK``. A database inode owned here may carry
    SQLite's POSIX record locks, which closing any descriptor of it releases.
    """

    if lock is not None and lock in _REGISTRY:
        return True
    return database is not None and any(
        held.database == database for held in _REGISTRY.values()
    )


def admit_request(path: object, mode: object) -> StoreRequest:
    """Admit exact built-in input before any filesystem access.

    A ``str`` subclass or a path object could run caller code while it is
    converted or compared, or yield a different spelling later.
    """

    if type(path) is not str:
        raise TypeError("A durable store path must be an exact str")
    if type(mode) is not str or mode not in ("create", "open"):
        raise ValueError("The open mode must be exactly 'create' or 'open'")
    if not path or "\x00" in path:
        raise StoragePathError("A durable store path must be non-empty without NUL")
    try:
        os.fsencode(path)
    except UnicodeError as error:
        raise StoragePathError(
            "A durable store path must be a filesystem name"
        ) from error
    head, name = os.path.split(path)
    if name in ("", ".", ".."):
        raise StoragePathError("A durable store path must end in a database file name")
    if name.lower().endswith((LOCK_SUFFIX, *SIDECARS)):
        # Never open another store's lock or SQLite sidecar as a database.
        raise StoragePathError(
            "A database file name cannot end in a lock or SQLite sidecar suffix"
        )
    if len(os.fsencode(name)) + _LONGEST_SUFFIX > _NAME_MAX:
        raise StoragePathError(
            "The database file name leaves no room for its sidecar file names"
        )
    return StoreRequest(head, name, "create" if mode == "create" else "open")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class _Plan:
    path: StoragePath
    existing: str
    missing: tuple[str, ...]


def _resolve(request: StoreRequest) -> _Plan:
    """Canonical directory: ``realpath`` of the deepest existing ancestor.

    Only ``create`` may continue below missing directories, and only through
    plain names; ``x/..`` below a missing ``x`` has no meaning to resolve.
    """

    head = request.head
    if os.path.isabs(head):
        probe = head
    else:
        probe = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), head) if head else os.getcwd()
    missing: list[str] = []
    while True:
        try:
            existing = os.path.realpath(probe, strict=True)
            break
        except FileNotFoundError:
            if request.mode == "open":
                raise StorageNotFoundError(
                    f"No durable store at {os.path.join(head, request.name)!r}: "
                    "its directory is missing"
                ) from None
            parent, part = os.path.split(probe)
            if part in ("", ".", "..") or parent == probe:
                raise StoragePathError(
                    "A missing directory cannot be followed by '.' or '..'"
                ) from None
            missing.append(part)
            probe = parent
        except NotADirectoryError:
            raise StoragePathError(
                "A parent path component is not a directory"
            ) from None
    if not os.path.isdir(existing):
        raise StoragePathError("A parent path component is not a directory")
    missing.reverse()
    directory = os.path.join(existing, *missing)
    return _Plan(StoragePath(directory, request.name), existing, tuple(missing))


def _lstat(path: str, dir_fd: int | None = None) -> os.stat_result | None:
    try:
        return os.stat(path, dir_fd=dir_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None


def _refuse_unusable(info: os.stat_result, label: str, *, by_name: bool = True) -> None:
    """Refuse a file that cannot be owned privately.

    ``by_name`` checks a file found by name, which this process must be able to
    open read-write. A file already open here (one it just created under a
    restrictive umask, say) only needs ``fchmod``.
    """

    if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):
        raise UnsupportedStoragePath(f"The {label} is a symbolic link")
    if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
        raise UnsupportedStoragePath(f"The {label} is not a regular file")
    if info.st_uid != os.geteuid():
        raise UnsupportedStoragePath(f"The {label} belongs to another user")
    if info.st_nlink != 1:
        raise UnsupportedStoragePath(f"The {label} has {info.st_nlink} hard links")
    if by_name and info.st_mode & FILE_MODE != FILE_MODE:
        raise UnsupportedStoragePath(
            f"The {label} is not readable and writable by its owner"
        )


def _refuse_journal(path: StoragePath) -> None:
    # A durable store is WAL-only, so a rollback journal belongs to a crashed
    # foreign writer or an interrupted switch to WAL. SQLite would roll it back
    # into the database on its first read; refuse before anything opens it.
    raise UnsupportedStoragePath(
        f"The rollback journal {path.sidecar('-journal')!r} exists; the database"
        " may need recovery outside the durable store and is left untouched"
    )


def _park_if_claimed(
    fd: int, info: os.stat_result, held: _Held | None, label: str
) -> None:
    """Refuse a descriptor that reached a database another owner here claimed.

    The caller holds ``_REGISTRY_LOCK``. Closing the descriptor would drop that
    owner's SQLite locks, so it is parked on the owner and closed only when the
    owner releases, after its connection is closed. Claims never move, so a
    parked descriptor always references its owner's claimed inode.
    """

    key = (info.st_dev, info.st_ino)
    for other in _REGISTRY.values():
        if other is not held and other.database == key:
            other.parked.append(fd)
            raise StorageOwnershipError(f"The {label} is already open in this process")


def _open_unowned(
    name: str, dir_fd: int, info: os.stat_result, label: str, held: _Held | None
) -> int:
    """Open the existing store file ``info`` describes, read-only.

    The caller holds the registry lock until it closes the descriptor, so no
    owner can claim the inode and connect in between. The descriptor is
    identified before anything else: a racing rename may have put another
    owner's database under ``name`` since it was checked.
    """

    fd = os.open(name, _READ_FLAGS, dir_fd=dir_fd)
    now = os.fstat(fd)  # On failure the descriptor is left open, never closed.
    _park_if_claimed(fd, now, held, label)
    if (now.st_dev, now.st_ino) != (info.st_dev, info.st_ino):
        os.close(fd)
        raise UnsupportedStoragePath(f"The {label} changed while it was checked")
    return fd


def _check_existing(
    name: str,
    dir_fd: int,
    info: os.stat_result,
    check: ExistingCheck,
    label: str,
    wal: os.stat_result | None,
    held: _Held | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Run ``check`` on a read-only descriptor of the file ``info`` describes."""

    fd = _open_unowned(name, dir_fd, info, label, held)
    try:
        check(fd, label, 0 if wal is None else wal.st_size)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _refuse_sidecars(
    path: StoragePath, sidecars: dict[str, os.stat_result | None]
) -> None:
    for suffix, sidecar in sidecars.items():
        if sidecar is not None:
            _refuse_unusable(sidecar, f"SQLite file {path.sidecar(suffix)!r}")
            if suffix == "-journal":
                _refuse_journal(path)


def _precheck_existing(path: StoragePath) -> None:
    database = _lstat(path.database)
    if database is None:
        raise StorageNotFoundError(f"No durable store at {path.database!r}")
    _refuse_unusable(database, f"database {path.database!r}")
    _refuse_sidecars(
        path, {suffix: _lstat(path.sidecar(suffix)) for suffix in SIDECARS}
    )


def _precheck(plan: _Plan, mode: OpenMode) -> None:
    """Refusals by ``lstat`` alone: no effect, and no descriptor on the store."""

    if plan.missing:
        return
    path = plan.path
    if mode == "create":
        for suffix in ("", *SIDECARS):
            if _lstat(path.sidecar(suffix)) is not None:
                raise StorageExistsError(
                    f"Cannot create {path.database!r}: {path.name + suffix!r} exists"
                )
    else:
        _precheck_existing(path)
    lock = _lstat(path.lock)
    if lock is not None:
        _refuse_unusable(lock, f"lock file {path.lock!r}")


# Filesystem classification ----------------------------------------------------


class _DarwinStatfs(ctypes.Structure):
    """``struct statfs`` with 64-bit inodes (sys/mount.h, MFSTYPENAMELEN 16)."""

    _fields_ = [
        ("f_bsize", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("f_iosize", ctypes.c_int32),
        ("f_blocks", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("f_bfree", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("f_bavail", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("f_files", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("f_ffree", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("f_fsid", ctypes.c_int32 * 2),
        ("f_owner", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("f_type", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("f_flags", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("f_fssubtype", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("f_fstypename", ctypes.c_char * 16),
        ("f_mntonname", ctypes.c_char * 1024),
        ("f_mntfromname", ctypes.c_char * 1024),
        ("f_flags_ext", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("f_reserved", ctypes.c_uint32 * 7),
    ]


def darwin_verdict(fstypename: str, flags: int) -> str | None:
    """Refusal reason for a macOS mount, or ``None`` when it is supported."""

    if not flags & _DARWIN_MNT_LOCAL:
        return f"{fstypename or 'unknown'} is not a local filesystem"
    if fstypename not in _DARWIN_LOCAL_TYPES:
        return f"{fstypename or 'unknown'} is not a supported local filesystem"
    return None


@functools.cache
def _darwin_fstatfs() -> Any:
    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
    try:
        # x86_64 exports the 64-bit-inode layout under this name; arm64 only
        # has the plain symbol, which already uses it.
        fstatfs = libc["fstatfs$INODE64"]
    except AttributeError:
        fstatfs = libc["fstatfs"]
    fstatfs.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int, ctypes.POINTER(_DarwinStatfs)]
    fstatfs.restype = ctypes.c_int
    return fstatfs


def _darwin_filesystem(fd: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    result = _DarwinStatfs()
    if _darwin_fstatfs()(fd, ctypes.byref(result)) != 0:
        code = ctypes.get_errno()
        raise OSError(code, os.strerror(code))
    return result.f_fstypename.decode("utf-8", "replace"), int(result.f_flags)


def linux_mount_type(fdinfo: str, mountinfo: str) -> str:
    """The type of the mount an open descriptor lives on.

    The descriptor's ``mnt_id`` selects one mount table line exactly, so bind
    mounts, overmounts and escaped mount points need no path matching.
    """

    mount = next(
        (
            line.split()[1]
            for line in fdinfo.splitlines()
            if line.startswith("mnt_id:") and len(line.split()) == 2
        ),
        None,
    )
    if mount is None:
        raise UnsupportedStoragePath("The kernel does not report the directory's mount")
    for line in mountinfo.splitlines():
        before, separator, after = line.partition(" - ")
        fields = before.split()
        if separator and fields and fields[0] == mount and after.split():
            return after.split()[0]
    raise UnsupportedStoragePath(
        "The directory's mount is missing from the mount table"
    )


def linux_verdict(fstype: str) -> str | None:
    """Refusal reason for a Linux filesystem type, or ``None`` when supported."""

    if fstype in _LINUX_LOCAL_TYPES:
        return None
    return f"{fstype} is not a supported local filesystem"


def _linux_filesystem(fd: int) -> str:
    try:
        with open(f"/proc/self/fdinfo/{fd}", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            fdinfo = stream.read()
        with open("/proc/self/mountinfo", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            mountinfo = stream.read()
    except OSError as error:
        raise UnsupportedStoragePath(
            "Cannot classify the filesystem without /proc mount information"
        ) from error
    return linux_mount_type(fdinfo, mountinfo)


def classify_directory(fd: int) -> None:
    """Refuse shared, network and unclassifiable filesystems (Root decision D8)."""

    if _PLATFORM == "darwin":
        fstype, flags = _darwin_filesystem(fd)
        reason = darwin_verdict(fstype, flags)
    elif _PLATFORM.startswith("linux"):
        reason = linux_verdict(_linux_filesystem(fd))
    else:
        reason = f"durable stores are not supported on {_PLATFORM}"
    if reason is not None:
        raise UnsupportedStoragePath(
            f"Unsupported filesystem for a durable store: {reason}"
        )


# Directories, lock and database -----------------------------------------------


def _sync_directory(fd: int) -> None:
    """Make new directory entries durable; on macOS only F_FULLFSYNC flushes."""

    os.fsync(fd)
    full = getattr(fcntl, "F_FULLFSYNC", None)
    if _PLATFORM == "darwin" and full is not None:
        fcntl.fcntl(fd, full)


def _open_directory(plan: _Plan) -> int:
    """Classify the existing ancestor, then create missing directories 0o700."""

    fd = os.open(plan.existing, _DIRECTORY_FLAGS)
    try:
        classify_directory(fd)
        for part in plan.missing:
            fd = _make_directory(fd, part)
        return fd
    except BaseException:
        os.close(fd)
        raise


def _make_directory(parent: int, part: str) -> int:
    try:
        os.mkdir(part, DIRECTORY_MODE, dir_fd=parent)
        created = True
    except FileExistsError:
        created = False
    if created:
        # The umask may have removed owner bits; the name is ours to fix.
        os.chmod(part, DIRECTORY_MODE, dir_fd=parent)
    child = os.open(part, _DIRECTORY_FLAGS, dir_fd=parent)
    try:
        info = os.fstat(child)
        if info.st_uid != os.geteuid():
            raise UnsupportedStoragePath(
                f"The directory {part!r} belongs to another user"
            )
        if created:
            _sync_directory(parent)
    except BaseException:
        os.close(child)
        raise
    os.close(parent)
    return child


def _private_fd(fd: int, label: str) -> os.stat_result:
    """Check an open file and make it exactly owner read/write."""

    info = os.fstat(fd)
    _refuse_unusable(info, label, by_name=False)
    if stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) != FILE_MODE:
        os.fchmod(fd, FILE_MODE)
        info = os.fstat(fd)
        if stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) != FILE_MODE:
            raise UnsupportedStoragePath(
                f"The filesystem cannot keep the {label} owner-only"
            )
    return info


@functools.cache
def _pipy_version() -> str:
    try:
        return importlib.metadata.version("pipy")
    except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        return "unknown"


def _diagnostic() -> bytes:
    value = {
        "schema": 1,
        "pid": os.getpid(),
        "acquired_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
        "pipy": _pipy_version(),
    }
    return (json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True) + "\n").encode("ascii")


def _holder(fd: int) -> str:
    """Bounded diagnostic text from a held lock; it never decides anything."""

    try:
        value = json.loads(os.pread(fd, _DIAGNOSTIC_LIMIT, 0).decode("utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError, RecursionError):
        return ""
    pid = value.get("pid") if type(value) is dict else None
    return f" (lock diagnostic: pid {pid})" if type(pid) is int and pid > 0 else ""


def _gate_existing(dir_fd: int, path: StoragePath, check: ExistingCheck) -> None:
    """Check an existing database's format before its lock is taken.

    Under the registry lock, and only once neither its lock inode nor its
    database inode is owned by this process: owners claim both before they
    connect, so closing the read-only descriptor cannot release an owner's
    SQLite locks (see the module docstring on POSIX record locks).
    """

    label = f"database {path.database!r}"
    with _REGISTRY_LOCK:
        database = _lstat(path.name, dir_fd)
        if database is None:
            raise StorageNotFoundError(f"No durable store at {path.database!r}")
        _refuse_unusable(database, label)
        lock = _lstat(path.name + LOCK_SUFFIX, dir_fd)
        lock_key = None if lock is None else (lock.st_dev, lock.st_ino)
        if _owned_here(lock_key, (database.st_dev, database.st_ino)):
            raise StorageOwnershipError(
                f"The durable store {path.database!r} is already open in this process"
            )
        # By lstat only. Its size can only defer a decision to the checks under
        # the lock, which refuse a linked or foreign -wal before anything uses it.
        wal = _lstat(path.name + "-wal", dir_fd)
        _check_existing(path.name, dir_fd, database, check, label, wal)


def _claim_database(held: _Held, info: os.stat_result, path: StoragePath) -> None:
    """Claim this owner's database inode before it is opened or connected.

    The caller holds ``_REGISTRY_LOCK``. A claim is never moved to another
    inode: descriptors parked on this owner reference its claimed inode and
    stay covered by the claim until the owner releases. A name that now names
    another inode fails the open instead.
    """

    key = (info.st_dev, info.st_ino)
    if any(other is not held and other.database == key for other in _REGISTRY.values()):
        raise StorageOwnershipError(
            "The durable store's database is already open in this process"
        )
    if held.database is not None and held.database != key:
        raise UnsupportedStoragePath(
            f"The durable store {path.database!r} changed while opening"
        )
    held.database = key


def _after_lock() -> None:
    """Test seam between taking the flock and re-checking the lock file name."""


def _lock(dir_fd: int, path: StoragePath) -> _Held:
    name = path.name + LOCK_SUFFIX
    label = f"lock file {path.lock!r}"
    # Under the registry lock, which is also held across fork(), no lock
    # descriptor exists in this process without its registry record.
    with _REGISTRY_LOCK:
        try:
            fd = os.open(
                name,
                os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC | os.O_NONBLOCK,
                FILE_MODE,
                dir_fd=dir_fd,
            )
        except OSError as error:
            if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.EACCES):
                raise UnsupportedStoragePath(f"Cannot open the {label}") from error
            raise
        # Identified first, like every store descriptor: a rename may have put
        # another owner's database under the lock name.
        _park_if_claimed(fd, os.fstat(fd), None, label)
        try:
            info = _private_fd(fd, label)
            key = (info.st_dev, info.st_ino)
            database = _lstat(path.name, dir_fd)
            database_key = (
                None if database is None else (database.st_dev, database.st_ino)
            )
            if _owned_here(key, database_key):
                raise StorageOwnershipError(
                    f"The durable store {path.database!r} is already open in this process"
                )
            try:
                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
            except BlockingIOError:
                raise StorageOwnershipError(
                    f"The durable store {path.database!r} is owned by another process"
                    + _holder(fd)
                ) from None
            except OSError as error:
                raise UnsupportedStoragePath(
                    f"The filesystem refuses an exclusive lock on the {label}"
                ) from error
            _after_lock()
            current = _lstat(name, dir_fd)
            if current is None or (current.st_dev, current.st_ino) != key:
                raise StorageOwnershipError(
                    f"The {label} was replaced while it was being locked"
                )
            try:
                os.ftruncate(fd, 0)
                os.pwrite(fd, _diagnostic(), 0)
            except OSError:
                pass  # Diagnostic only: the held flock alone is the ownership.
            held = _Held(key, fd, os.getpid(), database_key)
            _REGISTRY[key] = held
            return held
        except BaseException:
            os.close(fd)
            raise


def _unlock(held: _Held) -> None:
    """Release a lock; the owner's connection, if any, is already closed."""

    with _REGISTRY_LOCK:
        if _REGISTRY.get(held.key) is held:
            del _REGISTRY[held.key]
        try:
            # LOCK_UN releases even if a stray inherited copy of this open file
            # description survives in a child that skipped the fork hooks.
            fcntl.flock(held.fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
        finally:
            os.close(held.fd)
            # Still under the registry lock, so nobody claims and connects first.
            while held.parked:
                os.close(held.parked.pop())


def _normalize(
    dir_fd: int, name: str, info: os.stat_result, label: str, held: _Held
) -> os.stat_result:
    _refuse_unusable(info, label)
    if stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) == FILE_MODE:
        return info
    fd = _open_unowned(name, dir_fd, info, label, held)
    try:
        return _private_fd(fd, label)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _create_database(dir_fd: int, path: StoragePath, held: _Held) -> os.stat_result:
    for suffix in ("", *SIDECARS):
        if _lstat(path.name + suffix, dir_fd) is not None:
            raise StorageExistsError(
                f"Cannot create {path.database!r}: {path.name + suffix!r} exists"
            )
    try:
        fd = os.open(
            path.name,
            os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC,
            FILE_MODE,
            dir_fd=dir_fd,
        )
    except FileExistsError:
        raise StorageExistsError(
            f"Cannot create {path.database!r}: it exists"
        ) from None
    made: tuple[int, int] | None = None
    try:
        try:
            first = os.fstat(fd)
            made = (first.st_dev, first.st_ino)
            with _REGISTRY_LOCK:  # A new inode: nobody here can hold locks on it.
                _claim_database(held, first, path)
            info = _private_fd(fd, f"database {path.database!r}")
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
        # Inside the cleanup scope: a create whose new entry cannot be made
        # durable leaves nothing behind and can simply be retried.
        _sync_directory(dir_fd)
    except BaseException as error:
        if made is not None:
            _unlink_created(dir_fd, path.name, made, error)
        raise
    return info


def _unlink_created(
    dir_fd: int, name: str, identity: tuple[int, int], error: BaseException
) -> None:
    """Remove exactly the file this create made; keep ``error`` the cause."""

    try:
        current = _lstat(name, dir_fd)
        if (
            current is not None
            and stat.S_ISREG(current.st_mode)
            and (current.st_dev, current.st_ino) == identity
        ):
            os.unlink(name, dir_fd=dir_fd)
    except OSError as cleanup:
        error.add_note(f"Removing the new database also failed: {cleanup!r}")


def _open_database(
    dir_fd: int, path: StoragePath, check: ExistingCheck | None, held: _Held
) -> tuple[os.stat_result, int]:
    """Re-check an existing database under the lock, then make it owner-only.

    The database inode is claimed before any descriptor opens it, and this
    owner has not connected yet; every descriptor is opened and closed under
    one registry lock hold (see the module docstring on POSIX record locks).
    """

    database = _lstat(path.name, dir_fd)
    if database is None:
        raise StorageNotFoundError(f"No durable store at {path.database!r}")
    label = f"database {path.database!r}"
    _refuse_unusable(database, label)
    sidecars = {suffix: _lstat(path.name + suffix, dir_fd) for suffix in SIDECARS}
    _refuse_sidecars(path, sidecars)
    with _REGISTRY_LOCK:
        _claim_database(held, database, path)
        if check is not None:
            # Before any mode change, so a refused file keeps its bytes and mode.
            wal = sidecars["-wal"]
            _check_existing(path.name, dir_fd, database, check, label, wal, held)
        info = _normalize(dir_fd, path.name, database, label, held)
        wal_size = 0
        for suffix, sidecar in sidecars.items():
            if sidecar is not None:
                label = f"SQLite file {path.sidecar(suffix)!r}"
                sidecar = _normalize(dir_fd, path.name + suffix, sidecar, label, held)
                if suffix == "-wal":
                    wal_size = sidecar.st_size
    return info, wal_size


class PathOwner:
    """The exclusive owner of one canonical durable store path.

    ``close()`` is idempotent. In a process forked from the owner, every
    operation raises ``StorageForkedError`` and ``close()`` does nothing: the
    fork hook already closed the child's copy of the lock, and the child owns
    nothing.
    """

    __slots__ = (
        "path",
        "created",
        "database_identity",
        "directory_identity",
        "wal_size_at_open",
        "_held",
        "_lock",
        "_closed",
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        path: StoragePath,
        held: _Held,
        *,
        created: bool,
        database: os.stat_result,
        directory: os.stat_result,
        wal_size: int,
    ) -> None:
        self.path = path
        self.created = created
        self.database_identity = (database.st_dev, database.st_ino)
        self.directory_identity = (directory.st_dev, directory.st_ino)
        # Bytes of a -wal file found under the lock before any connection:
        # non-zero means the previous owner did not close cleanly (D6 input).
        self.wal_size_at_open = wal_size
        self._held = held
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._closed = False

    @property
    def forked(self) -> bool:
        return self._held.pid != os.getpid()

    @property
    def lock_fd(self) -> int:
        return self._held.fd

    def check_usable(self) -> None:
        if self.forked:
            raise StorageForkedError(
                "A durable store owner cannot be used after fork()"
            )
        with self._lock:
            if self._closed:
                raise StorageClosedError("The durable store owner is closed")

    def pin_in_forked_children(self, value: object) -> None:
        """Keep ``value`` from ever being finalized in a forked child."""

        with _REGISTRY_LOCK:
            self._held.pinned.append(value)

    def discard_created_files(self) -> None:
        """After a failed ``create``, remove the database and sidecars it made.

        Only files this owner created exist under its lock (``create`` refused
        any existing database or sidecar). The lock file and any created
        directories stay.
        """

        self.check_usable()
        if not self.created:
            return
        fd = os.open(self.path.directory, _DIRECTORY_FLAGS)
        try:
            info = os.fstat(fd)
            if (info.st_dev, info.st_ino) != self.directory_identity:
                raise UnsupportedStoragePath("The store directory changed while open")
            for suffix in SIDECARS:
                sidecar = _lstat(self.path.name + suffix, fd)
                if sidecar is not None and stat.S_ISREG(sidecar.st_mode):
                    self._check_created(fd)
                    os.unlink(self.path.name + suffix, dir_fd=fd)
            self._check_created(fd)
            os.unlink(self.path.name, dir_fd=fd)
            _sync_directory(fd)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)

    def _check_created(self, fd: int) -> None:
        """Right before an unlink by name: the name still names this create's file.

        Best-effort (see the contract boundary): a replacement that arrives
        between this check and the unlink is not seen.
        """

        database = _lstat(self.path.name, fd)
        if (
            database is None
            or (database.st_dev, database.st_ino) != self.database_identity
        ):
            raise UnsupportedStoragePath(
                f"The durable store {self.path.database!r} changed while open"
            )

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self.forked:
            return
        with self._lock:
            if self._closed:
                return
            self._closed = True
            _unlock(self._held)


def acquire(request: StoreRequest, *, check: ExistingCheck | None = None) -> PathOwner:
    """Own the canonical path of an admitted request, creating it for ``create``.

    ``check`` validates an existing database's format (``open``) on a read-only
    descriptor twice: before the lock, so a refused file gets no lock file or
    other effect, and again under the lock before any change. Each time it also
    gets the size of the ``-wal`` by ``lstat`` (no descriptor), which tells that
    the previous owner did not close cleanly. Neither read
    happens until the in-process ownership check has excluded another owner of
    the lock or database inode (see the module docstring on POSIX locks).
    """

    plan = _resolve(request)
    _precheck(plan, request.mode)
    dir_fd = _open_directory(plan)
    try:
        directory = os.fstat(dir_fd)
        if request.mode == "open" and check is not None:
            _gate_existing(dir_fd, plan.path, check)
        held = _lock(dir_fd, plan.path)
        try:
            if request.mode == "create":
                database, wal_size = _create_database(dir_fd, plan.path, held), 0
            else:
                database, wal_size = _open_database(dir_fd, plan.path, check, held)
        except BaseException:
            _unlock(held)
            raise
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)
    return PathOwner(
        plan.path,
        held,
        created=request.mode == "create",
        database=database,
        directory=directory,
        wal_size=wal_size,
    )


def acquire_path(path: object, mode: object) -> PathOwner:
    """Admit, resolve and own a durable store path (see ``acquire``)."""

    return acquire(admit_request(path, mode))


# fork() ------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _pin_forever(values: list[object]) -> None:
    """Leak one reference to each value for the rest of this (child) process.

    The child never finalizes an inherited SQLite connection, which would run
    ``sqlite3_close`` against files that later owners may have replaced.
    """

    for value in values:
        ctypes.pythonapi.Py_IncRef(ctypes.py_object(value))


def _fork_prepare() -> None:
    # Held across fork() so the child never inherits a half-registered lock;
    # a with-block cannot span the before and after hooks.
    _REGISTRY_LOCK.__enter__()


def _fork_parent() -> None:
    _REGISTRY_LOCK.__exit__(None, None, None)


def _fork_child() -> None:
    global _REGISTRY_LOCK
    # The inherited lock is held by the forking thread's prepare hook.
    _REGISTRY_LOCK = threading.Lock()
    inherited = list(_REGISTRY.values())
    _REGISTRY.clear()
    for held in inherited:
        _pin_forever(held.pinned)
        # Closing (never LOCK_UN) these copies leaves the parent's locks held:
        # flock belongs to the shared description, record locks to the parent.
        for fd in (held.fd, *held.parked):
            try:
                os.close(fd)
            except OSError:
                pass


os.register_at_fork(
    before=_fork_prepare, after_in_parent=_fork_parent, after_in_child=_fork_child
)

"""Schema v1, migrations and open-time integrity of the durable store (DE03b).

Private and not exported. ``sqlite_connection.open_owned_database`` runs this
module on every ``create`` and ``open``; Storage semantics follow in DE03c.

Schema v1 has the shape of Pi durable 1.3.0's SQLite schema version 2 (tasks
with the ``sleeping`` status), Pi's table, index and column names and no table
prefix (Root decisions D7 and D11), plus these Python deltas (D1, D2):

- The payload columns, ``record`` in every record table and
  ``document_revisions.content``, are ``BLOB`` instead of ``TEXT CHECK
  (json_valid(...))``. DE03c stores UTF-8 JSON that keeps lone surrogates
  (``surrogatepass``) there: lossless for every owned value, and no JSON1
  functions (SQLite before 3.45 rejects BLOB arguments to them).
- ``document_revisions.version`` is a ``BLOB`` holding the version's JSON
  number instead of an ``INTEGER``, so a raw Storage version keeps ``0``,
  ``-1``, ``1.5``, ``-0.0`` and integers beyond 64 bits, as MemoryStorage does.
- ``durable_metadata.next_id`` is an ``INTEGER``; Pi's ``TEXT`` works around
  ``node:sqlite`` refusing integers beyond JavaScript's safe range.
- ``submission_requests`` maps a conversation's request ID to the submission
  that wrote it last, for MemoryStorage's last-writer rule without fallback
  (D2); Pi's SQLite backend returns the lowest matching ID instead.
- Tasks are created in their final shape, without Pi's version 1 to 2 rebuild.
- The database header names the store: ``application_id`` is ``0x50495059``
  ("PIPY") and ``user_version`` is the schema version, so the gate can refuse
  foreign and newer files before SQLite opens them.

The identity columns (task ``kind``, ``request_id``, document ``kind`` and
``key_value``) stay ``TEXT``; DE03c fills them with ASCII JSON (D1). Names come
from ``TABLES`` and ``INDEXES``, Pi's immutable identifier history, so a prefix
could still be added later.

Migrations, a port of Pi chord's ``applySqliteMigrations``. ``MIGRATIONS`` is
append-only: a released migration is never edited or removed, and versions are
contiguous from 1, which is checked before the database is touched. One
``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` transaction creates ``durable_schema`` when it is missing,
reads its version, refuses a newer one, and applies every pending migration
with its version bump (``durable_schema`` and ``user_version``; version 1 also
sets ``application_id``). Any error rolls all of it back and is raised
unchanged; a failed rollback raises ``SqliteRollbackError`` with both errors.
A crash leaves the old version, because SQLite discards an uncommitted
transaction, and the next ``open`` migrates again. Migrations run only under
the path lock; a read-only inspection (DE10) validates without migrating. A
change to what stored bytes mean, such as DE04b1b's first current delta
revision, needs a new version even without new DDL, so that older pipy refuses
the store instead of misreading it. Full histories/as-of/fork/migrations remain
DE27.

Open-time integrity. Before any connection the gate in ``sqlite_connection``
reads the header through ownership's descriptor rule and ``check_identity``
refuses a foreign application ID, a newer ``user_version`` and an interrupted
create, leaving every byte unchanged. The database file's header lags the
``-wal``: the identity and ``user_version`` reach the file only at a checkpoint.
So after an unclean shutdown (a non-empty ``-wal`` found under the lock before
connecting) the caller validates on a read-only connection after WAL recovery,
which also catches a newer version committed only in the ``-wal``, and the gate
lets one shape through to that check: a one-page database without identity or
schema next to a non-empty ``-wal``. ``validate_store`` requires, on a
connection, the identity again, the exact ``sqlite_schema`` objects of the
store's version (no extra table, index, view or trigger; the SQL text of each
object as replaying the migrations in memory produces it), a ``durable_schema``
version equal to ``user_version``, and a metadata singleton with ``2 <= next_id
<= 2**53`` and ``1 <= next_seq <= 2**53``. ``quick_check`` runs only after an
unclean shutdown (Root decision D6). Records are decoded and checked when they
are read (DE03c), not here. ``damage_as_corruption`` raises SQLite's corruption
errors (``SQLITE_CORRUPT`` with its extended codes, ``SQLITE_NOTADB``) as
``StorageCorruption`` wherever a store is opened, validated, migrated or closed;
other errors pass unchanged, and DE03c wraps its own statements the same way.
Stored values are read through ``typed_columns`` and ``typed_values``: each
column's storage class is read with it and must be exactly the class its
declared type allows (``integer``, ``text`` or ``blob``, and ``null`` only
where the column is nullable) before anything is decoded, and no value goes
through ``sqlite3``'s own text decoding, whose error is not SQLite's: text is
read as bytes and decoded strictly. STRICT tables keep the classes, but SQL
alone can store another one by rewriting a table's schema and restoring it, and
SQLite's own ``sqlite_schema`` has no STRICT at all; any other class, or text
that is not UTF-8, in the schema, the version or the counters is
``StorageCorruption``.

Recovery rule for an interrupted create. ``create`` makes an empty file, SQLite
writes a one-page WAL header into it, and one transaction then commits the
identity, the schema and the metadata. A crash before that commit leaves an
empty or zero-filled file, or a one-page database without application ID,
user version or schema. ``open`` refuses such a file (``InterruptedCreateError``)
and ``create`` refuses any existing file; nothing is adopted silently, because
nothing proves that this process's create made it and an empty foreign
database looks the same. The documented procedure: while no process owns the
store, remove the database and any ``-wal``, ``-shm`` and ``-journal`` next to
it (the lock file may stay), then create again; no committed data can be lost.
A crash after the commit leaves a complete store whose identity may still sit
only in the ``-wal``; ``open`` recovers and validates it and opens it normally.
Pi opens or creates and would adopt an empty or even a foreign file.

Sources: Pi durable 1.3.0 at 2ec55d808d455b1a64a2bf7888198207a096120a,
``packages/durable/src/storage/sqlite/migrations.ts`` (blob
a5ee244ae9e206d8b9a2e911dee5ca0749036d9c, sha256
dd0f6445e308133d86e7f9fac5945b0907b78f6a9012800ec53787f526d0dea9),
``packages/durable/src/storage/sqlite/schema.ts`` (blob
b807ba52910cb370426dc21d7dc40c9b2495e85e),
``packages/chord/src/sqlite/migrations.ts`` (blob
d4dc7efe88c2142af3ff281bebf56df72c87e1fb, sha256
bd21356d008b67c1c9c2da00bb49fcf439822d0fe8c2afaa17fac075474bbc40) and the
metadata check of ``packages/durable/src/storage/sqlite/storage.ts`` (blob
7dc5903828740fe278fdc692ef9f40dbf68982c7). MIT Copyright (c) 2025 Mario
Zechner; notice: tests/fixtures/durable/UPSTREAM-LICENSE.txt.
"""

class StoreIdentityError(RuntimeError):
    """The file is not a durable store this pipy can open (bytes unchanged)."""


class ForeignStoreError(StoreIdentityError):
    """Another application's, or no application's, SQLite database."""


class NewerStoreError(StoreIdentityError):
    """A durable store with a schema version newer than this pipy supports."""


class InterruptedCreateError(StoreIdentityError):
    """A file a crashed ``create`` left before its schema was committed."""


class StorageCorruption(RuntimeError):
    """The store contradicts its own schema or format; it is never repaired."""


class SqliteRollbackError(RuntimeError):
    """A transaction failed and so did its rollback; ``error`` is the first."""

    def __init__(self, error: BaseException, rollback_error: BaseException) -> None:
        super().__init__("SQLite transaction failed and rollback failed")
        self.error = error
        self.rollback_error = rollback_error


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Migration:
    """One schema version: SQL statements run in order, one per entry."""

    version: int
    statements: tuple[str, ...]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if type(self.version) is not int or self.version < 1:
            raise ValueError("A migration version must be an exact int of at least 1")
        if type(self.statements) is not tuple or any(
            type(statement) is not str for statement in self.statements
        ):
            raise TypeError("Migration statements must be a tuple of exact str")


def _schema_table() -> str:
    return f"""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {TABLES["durable_schema"]} (
        singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (singleton = 1),

            VALUES (1, 2, 1)""",
        f"""CREATE TABLE {t["record_ids"]} (

                ('conversation', 'entry', 'task', 'submission', 'document'))
        ) STRICT""",
        f"""CREATE TABLE {t["conversations"]} (

        ) STRICT""",
        f"""CREATE INDEX {i["conversations_by_owner_conversation"]}

        f"""CREATE INDEX {i["conversations_by_owner_task"]}
            ON {t["conversations"]} (owner_task_id, id)""",
        f"""CREATE TABLE {t["entries"]} (

        ) STRICT""",
        f"""CREATE INDEX {i["entries_by_conversation"]}
            ON {t["entries"]} (conversation_id, id DESC)""",
        f"""CREATE INDEX {i["entry_heads_by_conversation"]}
            ON {t["entries"]} (conversation_id, id DESC) WHERE head IS NOT NULL""",
        f"""CREATE TABLE {t["tasks"]} (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            conversation_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
            kind TEXT NOT NULL,

# Append-only. Tests and children replace it to exercise later versions.
MIGRATIONS: tuple[Migration, ...] = (Migration(1, _version_1(TABLES, INDEXES)),)


def _active(migrations: object = None) -> tuple[Migration, ...]:
    """Admit a migration list (``MIGRATIONS`` when ``None``) before any SQL."""

    if migrations is None:
        migrations = MIGRATIONS
    if type(migrations) is not tuple or any(
        type(migration) is not Migration for migration in migrations
    ):
        raise TypeError("Migrations must be a tuple of Migration")
    for index, migration in enumerate(migrations):
        if migration.version != index + 1:
            raise ValueError(
                "SQLite migrations must have contiguous versions starting at 1"
            )
    return migrations


def _target(migrations: tuple[Migration, ...]) -> int:
    return migrations[-1].version if migrations else 0


def _newer(version: int, supported: int) -> str:
    # Pi chord's message, word for word.
    return (
        f"SQLite schema version {version} is newer than supported version {supported}"
    )


def _interrupted(label: str) -> str:
    return (
        f"The {label} is an interrupted create that never committed a schema;"
        " while no process owns the store, remove it and any -wal, -shm and"
        " -journal next to it, then create the store again"
    )


def _foreign(label: str, application: int, version: int) -> str:
    return (
        f"The {label} is not a pipy durable store (application ID"
        f" {application & 0xFFFFFFFF:#010x}, user version {version})"
    )


def _one_empty_page(header: bytes, size: int) -> bool:
    """Exactly one page and no schema: what the WAL switch of a create writes."""

    raw = int.from_bytes(header[16:18], "big")
    page = MAX_PAGE_SIZE if raw == 1 else raw
    return size == page and int.from_bytes(header[40:44], "big") == 0


def check_unwritten(data: bytes, size: int, label: str) -> None:
    """Refuse a file a create left before SQLite wrote its first page.

    ``data`` holds the first ``min(size, MAX_PAGE_SIZE)`` bytes: an empty file,
    or one page at most of zeros (a torn first write), is no database at all.
    """

    if size <= MAX_PAGE_SIZE and not data.strip(b"\x00"):
        raise InterruptedCreateError(_interrupted(label))


def check_identity(header: bytes, size: int, label: str, wal_size: int) -> None:
    """The pre-connect identity gate on a valid WAL header (bytes 60-63, 68-71).

    A one-page database without identity or schema and with a non-empty
    ``-wal`` passes: the create's first migration may have committed into the
    ``-wal`` only, so the caller decides after WAL recovery, on a read-only
    connection. Every other refusal happens here, before SQLite sees the file.
    """

    application = int.from_bytes(header[68:72], "big", signed=True)
    version = int.from_bytes(header[60:64], "big", signed=True)
    supported = _target(_active())
    if application == APPLICATION_ID:
        if version > supported:
            raise NewerStoreError(_newer(version, supported))
        if version < 1:
            raise StorageCorruption(
                f"The {label} has the durable store's application ID but no"
                " schema version"
            )
        return
    if application == 0 and version == 0 and _one_empty_page(header, size):
        if wal_size > 0:
            return
        raise InterruptedCreateError(_interrupted(label))
    raise ForeignStoreError(_foreign(label, application, version))


Objects = frozenset[tuple[str, str, str, str | None]]


# The storage classes a column may hold, as ``typeof`` names them.
INTEGER = frozenset({"integer"})
NULLABLE_INTEGER = frozenset({"integer", "null"})
TEXT = frozenset({"text"})
NULLABLE_TEXT = frozenset({"text", "null"})
BLOB = frozenset({"blob"})


def typed_columns(*names: str) -> str:
    """Result columns for ``names``: each column's storage class, then its value.

    ``sqlite3`` never decodes a value (its error is not SQLite's, so
    ``damage_as_corruption`` would pass it on, and it quotes the stored text):
    text is read as bytes, for ``typed_values`` to decode once the class holds.
    """

    return ", ".join(
        f"typeof({name}), CASE typeof({name}) WHEN 'text'"
        f" THEN CAST({name} AS BLOB) ELSE {name} END"
        for name in names
    )


def typed_values(
    row: Sequence[object],
    classes: Sequence[frozenset[str]],
    refuse: Callable[[int, str], StorageCorruption],
) -> tuple[object, ...]:
    """The values of a ``typed_columns`` row, each of exactly its allowed classes.

    Every storage class is checked before anything is decoded; then text is
    decoded strictly. ``refuse(column, problem)`` makes the error, whose problem
    names storage classes only, never stored data.
    """

    stored, values = row[0::2], row[1::2]
    for index, (found, allowed) in enumerate(zip(stored, classes, strict=True)):
        if found not in allowed:
            permitted = " or ".join(sorted(allowed))
            raise refuse(index, f"holds {found} where the schema allows {permitted}")
    decoded: list[object] = []
    for index, (found, value) in enumerate(zip(stored, values, strict=True)):
        if found == "text":
            try:
                value = cast(bytes, value).decode("utf-8")
            except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
                raise refuse(index, "is not UTF-8") from error
        decoded.append(value)
    return tuple(decoded)


# SQLite's own schema table: text, and no SQL for automatic indexes.
SCHEMA_COLUMNS = (
    ("type", TEXT),
    ("name", TEXT),
    ("tbl_name", TEXT),
    ("sql", NULLABLE_TEXT),
)
_SCHEMA_ROWS = (
    f"SELECT {typed_columns(*(name for name, _ in SCHEMA_COLUMNS))} FROM sqlite_schema"
)


def _schema_refusal(column: int, problem: str) -> StorageCorruption:
    return StorageCorruption(
        f"The durable store's schema column {SCHEMA_COLUMNS[column][0]} {problem}"
    )


def _objects(connection: sqlite3.Connection) -> Objects:
    rows = connection.execute(_SCHEMA_ROWS).fetchall()
    classes = [allowed for _, allowed in SCHEMA_COLUMNS]
    return frozenset(
        cast(
            tuple[str, str, str, str | None],
            typed_values(row, classes, _schema_refusal),
        )
        for row in rows
    )


@functools.cache
def _expected(migrations: tuple[Migration, ...]) -> Objects:
    """The objects of a store at the last of ``migrations``, replayed in memory.

    Replaying through the same SQLite reproduces its normalized SQL text,
    including the quoted names that ``ALTER TABLE ... RENAME`` writes.
    """

    memory = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", isolation_level=None)
    try:
        memory.execute(_schema_table())
        for migration in migrations:
            for statement in migration.statements:
                memory.execute(statement)
        return _objects(memory)
    finally:
        memory.close()


def _damaged(error: sqlite3.DatabaseError) -> bool:
    """SQLite's own corruption codes; errors the module raises carry no code."""

    code = getattr(error, "sqlite_errorcode", None)
    return type(code) is int and code & 0xFF in _DAMAGED


@contextlib.contextmanager
def damage_as_corruption(label: str) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Raise SQLite's corruption errors as ``StorageCorruption``, nothing else.

    ``SQLITE_CORRUPT`` with its extended codes and ``SQLITE_NOTADB`` become
    ``StorageCorruption`` with the SQLite error as the cause. Every other error
    passes unchanged, and so does one without an SQLite code (Python 3.11 and
    later set ``sqlite_errorcode`` on errors that come from SQLite; errors the
    ``sqlite3`` module raises itself have none), so nothing else is
    reclassified as damage.
    """

    try:
        yield
    except sqlite3.DatabaseError as error:
        if not _damaged(error):
            raise
        raise StorageCorruption(f"SQLite reports the {label} as damaged") from error


def _pragma(connection: sqlite3.Connection, name: str) -> int:
    value = connection.execute(f"PRAGMA {name}").fetchone()[0]
    if type(value) is not int:
        raise StorageCorruption(f"SQLite PRAGMA {name} is not an integer")
    return value


def _difference(found: Objects, expected: Objects, version: int) -> str:
    extra = sorted(f"{kind} {name}" for kind, name, _, _ in found - expected)
    missing = sorted(f"{kind} {name}" for kind, name, _, _ in expected - found)
    return (
        f"The durable store's schema does not match version {version}:"
        f" unexpected {extra[:5]}, missing or changed {missing[:5]}"
    )


# The columns read from the two singletons, with their storage classes.
VERSION_COLUMNS = (("version", INTEGER),)
METADATA_COLUMNS = (("next_id", INTEGER), ("next_seq", INTEGER))
_VERSION = (
    f"SELECT {typed_columns(*(name for name, _ in VERSION_COLUMNS))}"
    f" FROM {TABLES['durable_schema']} WHERE singleton = 1"
)
_METADATA = (
    f"SELECT {typed_columns(*(name for name, _ in METADATA_COLUMNS))}"
    f" FROM {TABLES['durable_metadata']} WHERE singleton = 1"
)


def _version(row: tuple[object, ...] | None) -> int:
    if row is None:
        raise StorageCorruption("SQLite schema metadata is missing")
    (version,) = typed_values(
        row,
        [allowed for _, allowed in VERSION_COLUMNS],
        lambda _, problem: StorageCorruption(
            f"SQLite schema metadata column version {problem}"
        ),
    )
    return cast(int, version)


def _stored_version(connection: sqlite3.Connection) -> int:
    return _version(connection.execute(_VERSION).fetchone())


def read_metadata(connection: sqlite3.Connection) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """The metadata singleton's ``(next_id, next_seq)``, refused unless in range."""

    row = connection.execute(_METADATA).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        # Pi durable storage.ts open(), word for word.
        raise StorageCorruption("Durable SQLite metadata is missing")
    next_id, next_seq = cast(
        tuple[int, int],
        typed_values(
            row,
            [allowed for _, allowed in METADATA_COLUMNS],
            lambda column, problem: StorageCorruption(
                f"Durable SQLite metadata column {METADATA_COLUMNS[column][0]}"
                f" {problem}"
            ),
        ),
    )
    if not (2 <= next_id <= _COUNTER_LIMIT and 1 <= next_seq <= _COUNTER_LIMIT):
        raise StorageCorruption("Durable SQLite metadata is out of range")
    return next_id, next_seq


def _validate(
    connection: sqlite3.Connection, migrations: tuple[Migration, ...], label: str
) -> int:
    supported = _target(migrations)
    application = _pragma(connection, "application_id")
    version = _pragma(connection, "user_version")
    objects = _objects(connection)
    if application != APPLICATION_ID:
        if application == 0 and version == 0 and not objects:
            raise InterruptedCreateError(_interrupted(label))
        raise ForeignStoreError(_foreign(label, application, version))
    if version > supported:
        raise NewerStoreError(_newer(version, supported))
    if version < 1:
        raise StorageCorruption(
            f"The {label} has the durable store's application ID but no schema version"
        )
    expected = _expected(migrations[:version])
    if objects != expected:
        raise StorageCorruption(_difference(objects, expected, version))
    stored = _stored_version(connection)
    if stored > supported:
        raise NewerStoreError(_newer(stored, supported))
    if stored != version:
        raise StorageCorruption(
            f"The durable store's schema version {stored} does not match its"
            f" header's user version {version}"
        )
    read_metadata(connection)
    return version


def validate_store(
    connection: sqlite3.Connection,
    migrations: tuple[Migration, ...] | None = None,
    *,
    label: str = "database",
) -> int:
    """Check a store's identity, exact schema and metadata; return its version.

    Reads only, so it serves read-only connections too. Damage that SQLite
    reports while reading becomes ``StorageCorruption``.
    """

    active = _active(migrations)
    with damage_as_corruption(label):
        return _validate(connection, active, label)


def quick_check(connection: sqlite3.Connection, *, label: str = "database") -> None:
    """``PRAGMA quick_check``; any finding refuses the store (D6)."""

    with damage_as_corruption(label):
        rows = connection.execute("PRAGMA quick_check").fetchall()
    if rows != [("ok",)]:
        raise StorageCorruption(
            f"quick_check found {len(rows)} problem(s) in the {label}, first:"
            f" {str(rows[0][0])[:200]!r}"
        )


def _before_statement(version: int, index: int) -> None:
    """Test seam: runs before each migration statement, inside the transaction."""


def roll_back(connection: sqlite3.Connection, error: BaseException) -> None:
    """Roll back after ``error``, only while a transaction is open.

    SQLite may already have rolled the whole transaction back (``SQLITE_FULL``,
    for example). Pi chord's rule: a failed rollback raises a different error,
    ``SqliteRollbackError`` carrying both.
    """

    if not connection.in_transaction:
        return
    try:
        connection.execute("ROLLBACK")
    except Exception as failure:
        raise SqliteRollbackError(error, failure) from failure


def _bootstrap(connection: sqlite3.Connection, target: int) -> int:
    schema = TABLES["durable_schema"]
    connection.execute(_schema_table())
    connection.execute(
        f"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO {schema} (singleton, version) VALUES (1, 0)"
    )
    version = _version(connection.execute(_VERSION).fetchone())
    if version > target:
        raise NewerStoreError(_newer(version, target))
    return version


def _apply(connection: sqlite3.Connection, migration: Migration) -> None:
    if migration.version == 1:
        # The store's identity commits with its first schema, never apart.
        connection.execute(f"PRAGMA application_id = {APPLICATION_ID}")
    for index, statement in enumerate(migration.statements):
        _before_statement(migration.version, index)
        connection.execute(statement)
    connection.execute(
        f"UPDATE {TABLES['durable_schema']} SET version = ? WHERE singleton = 1",
        (migration.version,),
    )
    connection.execute(f"PRAGMA user_version = {migration.version}")


def apply_migrations(
    connection: sqlite3.Connection,
    migrations: tuple[Migration, ...] | None = None,
    *,
    label: str = "database",
) -> int:
    """Apply every pending migration in one transaction; return the version.

    The list is checked before any SQL. Nothing pending commits an empty
    transaction, which writes nothing. Damage SQLite reports is raised as
    ``StorageCorruption`` after the rollback.
    """

    active = _active(migrations)
    target = _target(active)
    with damage_as_corruption(label):
        connection.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            version = _bootstrap(connection, target)
            for migration in active[version:]:
                _apply(connection, migration)
            connection.execute("COMMIT")
        except BaseException as error:
            roll_back(connection, error)
            raise
    return target


def prepare(
    connection: sqlite3.Connection, *, created: bool, label: str = "database"
) -> int:
    """Bring a newly connected store to ``MIGRATIONS``; return its version.

    ``create`` migrates the new, empty database. ``open`` validates first, so
    a foreign, newer, interrupted or corrupt store is refused before anything
    is written, then applies pending migrations. Either way the result is
    validated again.
    """

    migrations = _active()
    if not created:
        version = validate_store(connection, migrations, label=label)
        if version == _target(migrations):
            return version
    apply_migrations(connection, migrations, label=label)
    return validate_store(connection, migrations, label=label)

"""Verified SQLite connection lifecycle for an owned store (DE03a, DE03b).

Private and not exported; no Storage semantics (DE03c).
``open_owned_database`` admits its input, checks the SQLite runtime, takes path
ownership (``ownership.py``) and only then connects with ``mode=rw``, so SQLite
never creates the database itself and its sidecars inherit the owner-only mode.
Every PRAGMA is set explicitly and read back, because compile-time defaults
differ between builds (Ubuntu's SQLite enables ``secure_delete`` by default, the
macOS development build does not). ``create`` switches the new database to WAL;
``open`` requires an existing WAL database, so opening never rewrites a foreign
database's header. Close runs a TRUNCATE checkpoint, then closes the
connection, then releases the path lock, each step in ``finally``. The header is
read only through ownership's descriptor rule (see ``ownership`` on POSIX
record locks): never while a SQLite connection of this process may hold locks
on the file, since closing that descriptor would release them. The name is
checked against the claimed inode with ``os.stat`` under the lock, right after
connecting and after configuration, as best-effort detection under the
contract boundary below. Once connected, no descriptor of the database is
opened.

Schema and integrity (DE03b, ``sqlite_schema``). The header gate,
``check_store_header``, reads the header once through that descriptor rule and
refuses, before any connection, an interrupted create, a file that is not an
SQLite database in WAL mode, a foreign application ID and a newer schema
version, so SQLite never reads, recovers or checkpoints such a file. After an
unclean shutdown (a non-empty ``-wal`` found under the lock, Root decision D6)
a read-only connection validates the recovered store and runs ``quick_check``
before the owner connects: a read-only connection never checkpoints, so its
refusal leaves the database and ``-wal`` bytes unchanged (SQLite rebuilds only
its ``-shm`` index). It is closed before the owner's connection opens, so its
descriptors close while no other connection of this process holds locks on the
file. The owner's connection then runs ``sqlite_schema.prepare``: ``create``
migrates the new database, ``open`` validates first and applies pending
migrations only to a valid older store. Every corruption error SQLite reports
while a store is opened or closed (``SQLITE_CORRUPT`` with its extended codes,
``SQLITE_NOTADB``) is raised as ``sqlite_schema.StorageCorruption`` with the
SQLite error as its cause, after the same cleanup as any other failure; other
errors pass unchanged.

Contract boundary. The store directory is private to the owning user (owned by
that user, mode ``0700``; missing directories are created that way, and keeping
an existing one private is the caller's part). While any owner holds a store,
from the moment an open or create of it starts until its close has completed,
renaming, replacing, hard-linking or deleting any store file (the database, its
``-wal``, ``-shm`` and ``-journal``, and the lock file), by any actor, is
outside the contract. pipy detects some of these cases on a best-effort basis
(the identity checks under the lock, after connecting and after configuration;
the parking of descriptors that reach a claimed database; the re-check before
each unlink of a failed create) but guarantees nothing about them. SQLite's own
guidance is the same: do not rename, unlink or replace an open database or its
journal. With the store files left in place, the guarantees hold: one owner per
store across processes and within the process, owner-only file modes, no
descriptor of a store file held by another owner in this process is ever closed
by pipy, and invalid input, an ``open`` of a missing path and a store refused
before its lock is taken have no filesystem effect. Pi durable 1.3.0 has no
cross-process locking at all, so this remains strictly stronger than the
reference.

Connection settings follow Pi durable 1.3.0 ``packages/chord/src/sqlite/node.ts``
(blob b156477e8749c5b0315f0444396e82b8ee79a5bf, sha256
87eee26ec2cd23f0ec19fa785c4b985546d85cf791fd6454e75bbe643e6eac68):
``journal_mode=WAL``, ``wal_autocheckpoint`` 1000 pages, a 5000 ms busy timeout
and a ``wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`` before close. Python decisions: synchronous
``FULL`` with ``fullfsync``/``checkpoint_fullfsync`` on macOS for the product,
``NORMAL`` as Pi's class for parity and benchmark runs (Root decision D3);
``temp_store=MEMORY``, ``trusted_schema=OFF`` and, by Root decision,
``secure_delete=ON`` on every platform, so deleted content is overwritten with
zeros in the database's pages (old WAL frames keep earlier page images until a
checkpoint truncates the log); SQLite 3.37 or newer (STRICT tables) in
serialized threading mode. MIT Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner;
notice: tests/fixtures/durable/UPSTREAM-LICENSE.txt.
